Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study used co-design workshops with blind and low-vision music teachers and students (disabled stakeholders) to develop a proof-of-concept haptic wearable aimed at supporting music learning (clear utility focus) while explicitly exploring aesthetics and material experiences (fun/experience focus). This aligns best with a design that considers both fun and utility from the outset with diverse stakeholders, i.e., option 3.

        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The co-design workshop involved guided exploration, prompting questions, and structured activities (sensory bodystorming, ideating through making) rather than free play or rigid-rule games. This aligns best with semi-structured play, where participants explore within researcher-defined tasks and prompts.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The study is a pilot plus co-design workshop about music learning tools (vibrotactile feedback, materials, wearables) for blind and low-vision musicians. There is no game, contest, or probabilistic mechanism; participants ideate, discuss, and experience prototypes while playing instruments. Outcomes are not determined by chance but by participants’ skills, perceptions, and design input. This best matches an entirely skill-based activity.

        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The study focuses on a wearable haptic device to support blind and low-vision music learners, used in lessons and practice that occur within a broader social environment including teachers and other students. The technology supports individual practice (solo affordance) but is explicitly discussed in relation to social contexts and teacher integration, indicating a mix of solo and social affordances rather than purely solo or purely social use.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The study is a set of co-design workshops using vibrotactile cues with musicians; there is no structured game or turn system described. Participants play instruments while receiving vibrations and discuss materials and use cases. This interaction is effectively simultaneous rather than turn-based or phase-based, so option 5 (entirely simultaneous) is the closest fit.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The paper studies envisioned uses of musical haptic wearables (MHWs) for BLV music learning, such as non-verbal cues, temporal vibrotactile alerts, and aiding memorization. These are primarily one-way cues or alerts that can be delivered ahead of actions and do not require continuous real-time mutual interaction like a competitive or cooperative online game. The discussion of minor latency being negligible and cues being delivered in advance suggests mostly asynchronous interaction with some time-sensitive (quasi-synchronous) aspects during music performance or practice. Thus the design is best characterized as mostly asynchronous with a few synchronous affordances.

        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The study is a series of co-design workshops with blind and low-vision music teachers and learners, focused on collaboratively exploring and designing musical haptic wearables to support BLV music learning. There is no indication of any competitive or game-like mechanics; all activities (bodystorming, material exploration, ideation) are cooperative and jointly oriented toward shared design goals. Thus the interaction structure is entirely collaborative.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The study is a co-design workshop around a wearable haptic prototype for blind and low-vision musicians, not a multiplayer or adversarial game. There are no roles for multiple interacting players with shared rules; instead, researchers present materials and vibrotactile patterns and participants respond individually. This maps best to an entirely asymmetrical interaction structure (researcher/designer vs. participant/user), so option 5 is the closest fit among the game-based categories.
